description: Hi! I’m a Class 9 student interested in space, science, technology and new ideas. I enjoy making projects, learning new things and solving problems creatively. I’m looking for teammates who are interested in space and are ready to work together. Skills like coding, research, designing or presenting would be helpful, but you don’t need to be an expert. Let’s make something interesting and learn together!
summary:
Our project is called MARSWALK 360°. We made this model to show what exploring Mars might look like in the future. We created a small version of the Martian surface using simple materials like cardboard, paint, sand and stones. We also added mountains, a crater, a rover and a solar panel to make the model look more realistic.
The main idea of our project is to show how important maps are when exploring a planet like Mars. The surface of Mars is not the same everywhere. There are rocky areas, hills and craters, so astronauts would need to plan their routes carefully. A good map can help them understand the land, choose a suitable path and find interesting places to explore.
We chose this project because we wanted to learn more about Mars and how humans might explore it one day. While making it, we learned that even a small journey on another planet needs a lot of planning, information and teamwork.
details:
Our project, MARSWALK 360°, is about how humans might explore Mars in the future and why having a proper map is important. We made a digital presentation of a Martian landscape with hills, a crater, a rover, a solar panel and a sample route.
The main purpose of our project is to show how a map can help astronauts understand the surface of Mars before going on an exploration journey. Mars has many different landforms, so astronauts would need to study the area and plan their route carefully. A map using information from different NASA missions could help them find suitable paths, understand the surroundings and choose interesting places for research.
This idea could make future Mars journeys more organised and help astronauts make better decisions. We wanted to explain this in a way that is easy for everyone to understand.
We used Google Slides and digital document-making tools to prepare our project. We did not use any coding language or electronic hardware in this digital version.
What makes our project creative is the way we have presented the Martian surface visually and connected it with the idea of route planning. While preparing it, we thought about the terrain, possible obstacles, the role of rovers and the safety of future astronauts.
Through this project, we learned that exploring Mars is not just about reaching a place. It also takes proper planning, teamwork and a good understanding of the surroundings.
